div.div: أُزْمُولَةٌ (AA, S, K) and (S, K) some say (S) إِزْمَوْلَةٌ, (S, K,) the latter accord. to As and Sb and Ez-Zubeydee, (TA,) and ↓ إِزْمَوْلٌ , (S, TA,) which is said by IJ to be quasi-coordinate to جِرْدَحْلٌ, because the و in it is not a letter of prolongation, for the letter before it is with fet-h, (TA,) applied to a mountain-goat and to one of other animals, Vociferous: (AA, S, K, TA:) or the first, [or, app, any of the three,] applied to a mountain-goat, such as, when he runs, leans, or bears, on one side: so accord. to AHeyth: Fr explains the first or second as applied to a horse, meaning that runs swiftly: and in like manner to a mountain-goat. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
